rv.q: Welcome, if you dare, to the savage world of Anna K. Jacobs and Michael R. Jackson's Teeth , a dark and sharp new musical comedy adapted from Mitchell Lichtenstein's cult 2007 fright flick.
This iteration of Teeth has undergone light orthodontia that has left it tightened and brightened.
Both are fully evident in Sarah Benson’s production, even if they never blend into a satisfying whole.
The genius of Teeth is still intact in the show's new digs.
Its points about sexuality and consent, shame and religion are all well made and crystal clear – yet Jacobs and Jackson never baldly declare them outright. It's a tricky task – and they've nailed it.
Other than this cavity, Teeth has bite.
Teeth isn’t sure if it wants to shout this screed wholeheartedly or just mock it.

What’s most disappointing about “Teeth” is not its excesses, although these are deliberately in-your-face — the aggressively vulgar lyrics, the gory severed penises – but how the various elements of the show don’t completely hold together.
But even if patrons don’t exit Teeth clamoring for the score on an original cast album, many will appreciate it most of the time, as it hurtles along under Patrick Sulken’s conducting.
Coasting almost entirely on outrage, it's like a John Waters film without laughs.
Michael R. Jackson and Anna K. Jacobs’s new musical Teeth has bite.

The golden-voiced Alyse Alan Louis is still sensational as the sharp-toothed heroine who transforms from a sex-negative Promise ring-wearing innocent into an avenging angel that seems more like Freddy Kreuger in a baby-doll dress.
Jackson...gets right back on track with Teeth, a precious gift with plenty of bite.

cn.t: Critics praise this campy horror musical's infectious pop-rock score and star Alyse Alan Louis, applauding its sharp commentary on sexuality, consent, and purity culture delivered without being preachy, though some find it overly literal-minded.

vr.q: If you're in New York and you want to see something that'll like reformat your brain, go see Teeth.
I just was so confused throughout this whole musical.
